method: Load driven from INSIDE the cluster (k8s Job hitting the agent ClusterIP at http://agent:8000) — NO kubectl port-forward in the path. Deterministic governed tool path (POST /solve tool.pii: regex + Luhn + redaction + policy), no LLM. Token obtained from the in-cluster Keycloak with the Host header set to the agent's expected OIDC issuer. The per-subject 60/min anti-abuse rate limit was LEFT IN PLACE; each sweep level was paced 62s into a fresh window and kept to 50 requests so it is clean of 429s WITHOUT weakening the control.

cluster_shape.note: Single-node kind cluster: all 3 agent replicas AND all infra (Qdrant/Postgres/Keycloak/OpenFGA/Redis for every division) share this one host's CPUs. This — not the architecture — is the throughput wall.

headline.finding: Removing the kubectl port-forward lifted the ceiling from ~18 rps to ~30 rps; the port-forward was a real dev-rig bottleneck, not the system.

replica_scaling_at_concurrency_8.finding: 3 replicas deliver ~2.2x the throughput and ~half the p50 latency of 1 replica, on a SINGLE node — the agent is partly I/O-bound on OpenFGA/Qdrant/Redis, so replicas overlap that wait. On a multi-node cluster this scales closer to linear.

in_cluster_sweep_3_replicas.note: Per-level samples are small (50, to stay under the rate limit) so individual rps points are noisy; the signal is the ~30 rps plateau (the one-node CPU ceiling) and 0 errors / 0 429s throughout.

what_would_make_this_fully_production_re: Multi-node cluster (or real nodes) so replicas don't share one host's CPUs — then replica scaling approaches linear.

Raising (or per-tenant scaling) the 60/min anti-abuse rate limit to measure SUSTAINED throughput beyond burst windows — requires an explicit decision since it weakens a security control on a shared cluster.
A paid / self-hosted LLM endpoint to take the e2e /query path out of the NVIDIA free-tier cold-start + rate limit (the governed /solve path benchmarked here is already LLM-free).
